memory_candidates: In this repo, Lean files with `module` + `public import` (not `public meta import`) headers cannot embed permanent `#eval`/`#guard`/`native_decide` declarations (structural module-system limitation, documented at Cslib/Logics/Modal/Tableau/LoopChecking.lean's 'Sanity Checks' section). Kernel-level `rfl`/`decide` also fails on functions compiled via nested well-founded recursion (e.g. modalExpandBranchesGen's fuel-driven processNext) even at small argument magnitudes, independent of the module-system limitation. Workaround: chain single, non-recursive step functions (e.g. modalStepBranchGen) via explicit `let`/`bind`, which DO reduce fine under `rfl`/`decide`, to build a mechanized multi-step counterexample without touching the recursive driver.

When generalizing a driver-level top-loop induction (e.g. modalExpandBranchesGen_openBranch_accSourcesKnown in BDriver.lean) over an abstract per-(branch,acc) predicate P, the double-induction body is often already predicate-agnostic -- the generalization is a pure mechanical parametrization requiring no new proof insight, only careful signature threading of the step-preservation hypothesis.
